messages:
Evan: quick follow-up from the low-bit RFC — we still need to settle the runtime contract for operator-level fallbacks. do we want a single `precision_profile` id or explicit per-operator flags?

Sana: my vote is for per-operator flags. some layers (LN, qkv) are super sensitive and we should be able to mark them as `require_fp16` while allowing others to be int4.

Luca: per-operator is flexible but the runtime complexity skyrockets. the kernel selector would need to query a map on every op. could we do a two-tier approach: `profile_id` + optional overrides?

Priya: +1 to two-tier. also need to define artifact compatibility. if model.tar has `profile_v2.json` with overrides, Dedicated nodes must validate before accepting. otherwise silent mis-serves.

Yuri: product concern: customers will not understand many knobs. expose `profile_id` in API and keep overrides in advanced settings in the Console. default conservative mapping for public hosted.

Maggie: evaluation note — our current regressions detect whole-model drop. we need layer-granular evals to catch subtle hallucination modes introduced by mixing 8/4. I'll add a per-layer quality check to the eval harness.

Evan: good point. operationally we also need a fallback signal path: runtime detects quality-change -> emits `precision_degrade` telemetry with sample input + token-level confidence -> controller can trigger rollback to `profile_id: full_fp16`.

Luca: implementation detail: would prefer a light-weight sentinel rather than full sample payload. maybe include `example_hash` and store sample in a separate s3 bucket with retention TTL. avoids blowing up telemetry volume.

Priya: security note — those saved samples may contain PII. we need KMS-tagged storage and an opt-out for private deployments. add to the Private checklist.

ops-oncall: deploy-bot: can we have an automated canary that runs 1% traffic on new low-bit profiles and aborts if latency or degrade_rate > threshold? :robot_face:

deploy-bot: @ops-oncall canary job created: `lowbit-profile-canary`. runs 10k tokens/min for 24h on dedicated pool. alerts to #eng-oncall if degrade_rate > 1.5%.

Sana: another model artifact idea: store a compact `sensitivity_map` (layer -> float) produced at offline calibration. runtime can use it to auto-select overrides when a profile requests aggressive packing. keeps the API simple but lets runtime be smart.

Luca: I like `sensitivity_map` but we need a stable format: list of layer names + score. request `sensitivity_v1` in artifact metadata. runtime will reject unknown versions.

Yuri: document UX: Console should show a heatmap of sensitivity and a preview of expected latency/cost impact when toggling low-bit. helps customers make tradeoffs.

Maggie: plan for canary + eval: add a regression prompt set with high-sensitivity cases and run diff against baseline every hour during rollout. if any metric drifts beyond margin, auto rollback.

Priya: infra checklist: artifact validation on push, signed `profile_id`, per-tenant opt-outs, TTL for sample storage, KMS policy for sample access, and a privacy flag in model manifest. I'll draft infra PR.

Evan: action items: 1) Luca + Priya define runtime contract doc w/ two-tier profile + overrides and `sensitivity_v1` schema (due EOD Fri). 2) Maggie builds per-layer eval set and integrates into canary (due next Wed). 3) Yuri wires Console UX mockups for heatmap (sync next Tue). 4) Priya adds artifact validation checklist PR.

Sana: one more: add a graceful quality-degrade header to API responses so clients can detect when low-bit mode is active, e.g. `x-rd-quality: lowbit-warning` — but make it opt-in for Hosted.

Evan: agreed, opt-in only. ok thanks all, will capture in the RFC follow-up doc. :thumbsup:
